concepts.def: The law of conservation of mass states that no atoms are lost or made during a chemical reaction so the mass of the products equals the mass of the reactants.
A representation of a reaction using chemical formulae, with the reactants on the left of the arrow and the products on the right.
A symbol equation in which the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides of the equation, which is what conservation of mass requires.
A number written in normal script before a formula, which multiplies every atom in that whole formula. In 2Ca(NO3)2 the leading 2 doubles the entire formula unit.
A small number written after a symbol, or after a closing bracket, which multiplies only the atom or the bracketed group that it immediately follows.
The relative mass of an atom of an element, the building block from which a relative formula mass is assembled.
The relative formula mass (Mr) of a compound is the sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in the numbers shown in the formula.
In a balanced chemical equation the sum of the relative formula masses of the reactants in the quantities shown equals the sum of the relative formula masses of the products in the quantities shown.
The share of a compound's relative formula mass contributed by one element: the Ar of that element multiplied by the number of its atoms, divided by the Mr of the compound, then multiplied by 100.
A reaction vessel open to the surroundings, so a gaseous reactant can enter or a gaseous product can leave without being weighed on the balance.

concepts.term: Thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate
concepts.def: Heating breaks the carbonate down into the metal oxide and carbon dioxide; the carbon dioxide escapes into the atmosphere, leaving the metal oxide as the only solid product.

concepts.term: Particle model explanation of a mass change
concepts.def: An account of an apparent mass change in terms of gas particles entering the vessel from the air, or leaving it and dispersing among the particles of the air.
The doubt that always exists about the result of a measurement, present whenever a measurement is made, however good the apparatus and the technique.
The pattern formed by a set of repeated measurements, showing where the results cluster and which of them lie apart from the rest.
A measurement lying well outside the cluster formed by the others; it is spotted when the distribution is represented and is excluded from the mean.

concepts.term: Range as a measure of uncertainty
concepts.def: The difference between the largest and the smallest of a set of measurements, used about the mean as a measure of uncertainty and quoted as the mean plus or minus half the range.

mcqs.q: Which statement gives the law of conservation of mass?
options: No atoms are lost or made, so the products have the same mass as the reactants.
Mass stays the same only when the reaction is run inside a sealed vessel.
The number of molecules is unchanged, so the total mass cannot change.
Mass is conserved when a solid melts but not when it reacts chemically.
mcqs.explain: This is the law as the specification states it: the atom count is fixed, so the total mass is fixed.

mcqs.q: 8.0 g of magnesium is burned in an open crucible and 13.3 g of magnesium oxide is left. Which explanation is correct?
options: The heat energy taken in during the burning has added 5.3 g to the solid.
5.3 g of oxygen from the air has joined the magnesium in the crucible.
Extra magnesium atoms have been made, which is why the mass rose.
The law of conservation of mass fails because the crucible is open.
mcqs.explain: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO. The crucible is open, so oxygen enters and is weighed with the product: 13.3 - 8.0 = 5.3 g.

mcqs.q: A student writes H2 + O2 -> H2O and is told it is not balanced. Which change balances it correctly?
options: Change the product to H2O2 so that two oxygen atoms appear on the right.
Write a 2 in front of O2 so that four oxygen atoms become available.
Write a 2 in front of H2 and a 2 in front of H2O, leaving O2 alone.
Add one more oxygen atom to the right-hand side of the arrow.
mcqs.explain: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O gives four hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms on each side, changing only the multipliers.

mcqs.q: Why must a symbol equation be balanced?
options: So that the same number of molecules appears on both sides of the arrow.
So that the number of different substances shown matches on both sides.
So that the energy given out matches the energy taken in by the reaction.
No atoms are lost or made, so each element has equal atoms per side.
mcqs.explain: Balancing is the direct consequence of conservation of mass, stated in terms of the numbers of atoms of each element.

mcqs.q: In the formula 2Ca(NO3)2, what do the large 2 at the front and the small 2 after the bracket each do?
options: The front 2 shows two calcium atoms; the small 2 shows two nitrogen atoms.
The front 2 doubles the whole formula; the small 2 doubles the bracket only.
The front 2 doubles only the calcium; the small 2 doubles the oxygen.
Both 2s multiply every atom, so each count in the formula is doubled twice.
mcqs.explain: A multiplier in normal script applies to the entire formula unit; a subscript after a bracket applies to the bracketed group.

mcqs.q: Calculate the relative formula mass of Ca(OH)2. Relative atomic masses: Ca = 40, O = 16, H = 1.
options: 57, from adding 40, 16 and 1 with the bracket subscript ignored.
58, from doubling the hydrogen atoms but keeping one oxygen.
74, because the bracket doubles both the oxygen and the hydrogen.
114, from doubling every atom in the formula, the calcium included.
mcqs.explain: Mr = 40 + 2(16 + 1) = 40 + 34 = 74, the sum of the relative atomic masses in the numbers shown.

mcqs.q: The relative atomic mass of oxygen is 16. What is the relative formula mass of O2?
options: 16, since that is the relative atomic mass given for oxygen.
16, since writing O2 does not add any mass to the oxygen.
18, from adding 16 to the 2 written in the formula.
32, because the molecule contains two atoms of oxygen.
mcqs.explain: Mr is the sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in the numbers shown: 2 x 16 = 32.

mcqs.q: For 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO the reactants total (2 x 24) + 32 = 80. The Mr of MgO is 40. What is the product total?
options: 80, since the same atoms are present on each side.
40, because the relative formula mass of MgO is 40.
64, because the 2 in front multiplies only the magnesium.
48, because only the magnesium ends up in the solid.
mcqs.explain: The quantity shown is 2MgO, so 2 x 40 = 80, equal to the reactant total as a balanced equation requires.

mcqs.q: Ammonium nitrate is NH4NO3, with Mr = 80. The relative atomic mass of nitrogen is 14. What is the percentage by mass of nitrogen?
options: 22%, from the 2 nitrogen atoms among the 9 atoms in the formula.
17.5%, from using the mass of only one of the nitrogen atoms.
35%, because the two nitrogen atoms give 28 out of the total of 80.
70%, from doubling for the two nitrogen atoms a second time.
mcqs.explain: (2 x 14) / 80 x 100 = 35%, using the relative formula mass and relative atomic mass supplied.

mcqs.q: Which method gives the percentage by mass of an element in a compound?
options: Divide the number of atoms of that element by the total atoms, then x 100.
Divide the Mr of the compound by the Ar of that element, then x 100.
Divide the Ar of the element by the Mr of the compound, then x 100.
Multiply the Ar by the number of those atoms, divide by Mr, then x 100.
mcqs.explain: The standard route, using the relative formula mass and relative atomic masses the question supplies.

mcqs.q: A weighed piece of copper is heated in an open crucible. The mass of the solid increases. Why?
options: Oxygen from the air has combined with the copper to form copper oxide.
Heat energy absorbed from the flame has added to the mass of the metal.
The copper atoms expand as they get hot, so each one becomes much heavier.
New copper atoms are made as the reaction goes on in the crucible.
mcqs.explain: 2Cu + O2 -> 2CuO. The oxide is heavier than the metal because the oxygen taken from the air is now weighed with it.

mcqs.q: Copper carbonate is heated in an open test tube: CuCO3 -> CuO + CO2. The mass of the solid falls. Why?
options: Some of the solid has been burned away by the heat of the Bunsen flame.
Carbon dioxide escapes, leaving copper oxide as the solid.
Mass is lost from the tube, so mass is not conserved in this reaction.
Strong heating has destroyed some of the solid, so that part no longer exists.
mcqs.explain: In the thermal decomposition of a metal carbonate the carbon dioxide escapes into the atmosphere, leaving the metal oxide as the only solid product.

mcqs.q: Use the particle model to explain why the balance reading falls when a metal carbonate is heated in an open tube.
options: The particles left in the tube move further apart, so the solid weighs less than before.
Gas particles carry no mass of their own, so the reading falls as gas forms.
Particles are destroyed as the solid turns into a gas inside the hot tube.
Carbon dioxide particles leave the tube and mix into the air, so they are no longer weighed.
mcqs.explain: The particle-model account the specification asks for: the particles still exist, but they are no longer inside the system on the balance.

mcqs.q: A student reads 25.00 cm3 from a burette, working carefully. Which statement about that measurement is correct?
options: There is always some uncertainty about the result, however careful you are.
There is no uncertainty, because a burette is precise apparatus.
Uncertainty appears only if the student misreads the burette scale.
Uncertainty would disappear if the whole titration were repeated three times.
mcqs.explain: Whenever a measurement is made there is always some uncertainty about the result obtained.

mcqs.q: Five titres are 24.8, 25.0, 25.1, 25.0 and 27.4 cm3. How should this set of results be handled?
options: Include all five in the mean, because a measured result may never be dropped.
Plot all five, treat 27.4 as anomalous and leave it out of the mean.
Just take the mean and treat it as the exact result, since averaging removes any doubt.
Use a single titre, since a precise burette gives the exact volume.
mcqs.explain: Representing the distribution shows 27.4 lying well away from the cluster, which is how an anomaly is identified.

mcqs.q: Four titres have a mean of 25.0 cm3, a lowest value of 24.8 cm3 and a highest of 25.2 cm3. How should the result be quoted?
options: 25.0 plus or minus 0.4 cm3, quoting the whole range as the uncertainty.
Report all four titres separately, since no reading may be left out.
25.0 plus or minus 0.2 cm3, which is half the range of 0.4 cm3.
25.0 cm3 exactly, since averaging the titres removes the uncertainty.
mcqs.explain: The range 25.2 - 24.8 = 0.4 cm3 is used about the mean, so the uncertainty quoted is half of it.
